title: A support team
that lives
on your PC
hero.lede: Crewline runs six AI agents on your own computer. They answer customers by chat and phone, look up real orders, refund the small ones by your rules, and bring you the rest.

questions.title: Most of your inbox is the same five questions
questions.lede: Each one means opening your store, finding the order, checking a policy and typing something you've typed a thousand times.

shops.lede: We tested it on an e-bike shop. The questions it handles are the ones most online stores get, whatever they sell.

private.title: What customers tell you stays in the room
private.lede: Orders, addresses, voices and photos are all processed on your machine. The models download once. After that, Crewline answers with the network cable out.

setup.title: From install to first solved ticket
setup.lede: Plan on an afternoon, and most of that is waiting for the models to download.

steps.title: Install it
steps.text: One Windows installer. It opens on Fernway, a sample e-bike shop with orders, customers and a month of conversations, so you can press every button before you commit to anything.

steps.title: Clear the sample shop
steps.text: When you're ready, open Store data and choose Start over. A checklist appears and ticks itself off as you go.

steps.title: Let it pick the models
steps.text: Crewline reads your graphics card and memory, then recommends a size. One click downloads everything it needs.

steps.title: Tell it who you are
steps.text: Store name, opening hours, tone of voice, sign-off and languages. Every reply uses them.

steps.title: Bring your orders
steps.text: Export products, customers and orders from Shopify or WooCommerce and drop in the CSV files. Any spreadsheet works too. Import again tomorrow and nothing doubles up.

steps.title: Hand over your policies
steps.text: Returns, shipping, warranty, manuals, your FAQ. Agents quote these and cite the passage. If the answer isn't there, they say so and hand over.

steps.title: Write your rules
steps.text: Start from five templates or a blank page. A flow is a list of steps: find the order, check the date, refund it, ask you first.

steps.title: Try to break it
steps.text: Test any flow on real orders without sending a message or changing a thing. Then chat with it and call it the way a customer would.

steps.title: Run your day from one board
steps.text: Clear whatever's amber. See what the agents couldn't answer. Write that answer once and it's there for everyone after.

flows.title: Rules you could read out loud
flows.rule: Refund it by itself when the order is **$300** or less
flows.lede: A flow is a list of plain steps with the paths drawn between them. There's no code to write, and every step shows what it did and how long it took.

photo.title: It can see what arrived
photo.lede: A customer sends a photo of a torn box. A vision model on your PC describes the damage, the flow checks the order against your limit, and the replacement goes out.

quote.text: We're sorry to hear your order arrived damaged. The photo shows a torn box with scattered styrofoam. We're shipping a free replacement of the items on order 1270 today.
quote.cite: Written by the Orders & returns agent in 1.9 seconds

approve.title: You keep the last word
approve.lede: Anything over your limit stops and waits, with the order, the customer's words and the rule that stopped it on one card. Approve it, change the amount or decline. If you approve, Crewline records the refund and tells the customer.

image.alt: The same refund approved and the customer told

languages.title: Replies in the customer's language
languages.lede: List the languages your shop speaks. Agents answer in whichever one the customer used, flow messages included, and they leave order numbers and tracking numbers alone.

receipts.title: Every answer shows its working
receipts.lede: Click a citation and you get the sentence it came from. Open the trace and you see who did what, and how long it took. When the documents don't cover something, the agent says so and hands it to you.

image.alt: An answer about a child seat with a citation, and the Sources panel showing the exact passage highlighted.

hours.title: Someone will write at 11:40 tonight
hours.lede: After hours the agents keep tracking orders and starting returns. If something needs a person, the customer gets a straight answer about when you're back.

numbers.note: Measured on Fernway, our sample shop: 25 products, 150 customers, 281 orders, 21 conversations with scripted customer messages. The models were real and ran on one RTX 5070. Your shop will get different numbers.

said.title: What it wrote back
said.lede: We haven't got customer reviews, because nobody outside this project has used it yet. These are real exchanges from the test day: the customers were scripted and the replies are exactly what the models wrote.

compare.title: How it compares
compare.lede: A cloud chatbot is quick to set up. A helpdesk is familiar, and an agency gives you real people. None of them looks up the order and acts on it within your limits.

hardware.title: It runs on a computer you can buy at a shop

items.title: Light
items.text: Under 16 GB of memory, no graphics card. Qwen3 1.7B writes and Kokoro speaks.

items.title: Balanced
items.text: 16 GB of memory or a 6 GB graphics card. Qwen3 4B writes.

items.title: Best
items.text: A 10 GB graphics card and 16 GB of memory. Qwen3 8B writes, a reranker sharpens search, LFM3-Audio speaks.

items.question: Can customers reach it from my website today?
items.answer: Not yet. The chat and call widget runs inside the app, where you set up, test and train your agents. Connecting a live website, an inbox and a phone number is the next piece of work.

items.question: Is it connected live to Shopify?
items.answer: No. You import CSV exports from Shopify, WooCommerce or a spreadsheet. Importing a newer file updates what's there, so tracking stays current if you do it daily.

items.question: When it refunds someone, does the money move?
items.answer: Not yet. Crewline records the refund, cancellation or replacement and tells the customer. You still press the button in your store or payment provider.

items.question: Will it replace my team?
items.answer: It takes the repeat questions. Complaints, unusual cases and anything over your limits still come to a person, with the work already done.

items.question: Does it work on a Mac?
items.answer: Not today. There's a Windows installer. The models run on NVIDIA, AMD or the processor alone.

items.question: Does it need the internet?
items.answer: Only to download the app and the models. After that, it answers customers on your machine.

items.question: Can it make mistakes?
items.answer: Yes. Replies show their sources, a Reviewer checks each one first, and anything with real money behind it can wait for your click.

download.lede: In the 1950s machines took over routing the calls, and operators kept the ones that needed a person. Your shop can make the same trade this afternoon.
